instruction.text: Justin is making a fruit salad for his family. He has <mat><t-yellow>3</t-yellow>/<t-purple>7</t-purple></mat> of a watermelon and <mat><t-yellow>20</t-yellow>/<t-purple>35</t-purple></mat> of a pineapple. Which fruit does he have more of?

atoms.a: Multiply the numerator by the same factor.

atoms.b: Justin has more ((++pineapple watermelon)) in his fruit salad.

instruction.text: Liam and Sophie are comparing the lengths of two ropes. Liam’s rope is <mat><t-yellow>10</t-yellow>/<t-purple>18</t-purple></mat> of a metre long. Sophie’s rope is <mat><t-yellow>2</t-yellow>/<t-purple>3</t-purple></mat> of a metre long. Who has the longer rope, and by how much?

atoms.a: Multiply the numerator by the same factor.

atoms.b: Her rope is longer by <mat><gap>2</gap>/<t-purple>18</t-purple></mat> of a metre.

instruction.text: Ethan has a collection of marbles. He fills <mat><t-yellow>6</t-yellow>/<t-purple>9</t-purple></mat> of a red bag and <mat><t-yellow>76</t-yellow>/<t-purple>99</t-purple></mat> of a blue bag. Which bag is fuller?

atoms.a: Multiply the numerator by the same factor.

instruction.text: In a bakery, Mrs Johnson has baked three different pies. The apple pie is cut into three slices, the cherry pie into four, and the blueberry pie into six.

atoms.a: Write a fraction to represents one slice of each type of pie.
atoms.b:
Apple pie slice: 1/3

Cherry pie slice: 1/4

Blueberry pie slice: 1/6

hint.text: When the <t-yellow>numerator</t-yellow> is the same, the <t-purple>denominator</t-purple> determines the size of the fraction. The smaller the <t-purple>denominator</t-purple>, the larger the fraction.

instruction.text: Help Mrs Johnson arrange the slices of pies in order from the smallest to the largest slice.

parentBlock.title: Comparing and Ordering Fractions with Different Denominators
